Attached are a few sample request IDs and short logs I pulled from our gateway (ingress request ids: brz-11-6-8-1, brz-11-6-8-2). We need immediate assistance — this is impacting live payments.

Can Redwood confirm whether there's a regional LB/edge issue or if this looks like something on our config?

Thanks,
Claire Dawson

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 09:12:47 +0000
Subject: URGENT: Brizo Pay EU 502/503 spike — request exec attention and mitigation

Team — Claire at Brizo Pay is seeing a sustained wave of 502/503 responses in the EU region starting 08:45 UTC; customer retries are triggering 429s and throughput saturation on a subset of EU LB instances. Customer traffic pattern: a high-concurrency checkout batch from their European gateway.

Key asks:
- Marcus/Jonas: can you confirm whether this is LB-level saturation or an upstream instance failure? Any immediate mitigations (drain, rotate, emergency route) we can apply without impacting other tenants?
- Laura: this is customer-facing and may require an SLA credit path if it lasts >2 hours — I wanted you in the loop for potential exec comms.

I've attached the customer snippets they sent. Paging on-call now. I'll post a short timeline as we have it.

Thanks,
Soojin
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 09:31:10 +0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: Brizo Pay EU 502/503 spike — request exec attention and mitigation

On Mon, Nov 6, 2028 at 09:12 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — Claire at Brizo Pay is seeing a sustained wave of 502/503 responses in the EU region starting 08:45 UTC; customer retries are triggering 429s and throughput saturation on a subset of EU LB instances.

Quick summary from infra:
- Root cause (working hypothesis): retry amplification from Brizo Pay's gateway plus a recent healthcheck flapping window caused several EU frontends to mark downstream pools unhealthy. That reduced effective capacity and concentrated traffic on remaining instances, producing 502/503s and exponential retries manifesting as 429s.
- Confirmed: three EU LB frontends showed elevated 5xx ratios and short-lived connection errors to a downstream worker pool between 08:43–09:20 UTC.

Mitigations applied (09:20–09:30 UTC):
- Temporarily increased ingress concurrency safeguards for Brizo Pay routes to limit retry amplification (rate limit override).
- Drained two affected frontends and rotated traffic to healthy nodes in the same region.
- Bumped upstream keepalive and backoff thresholds to reduce 502s from flapping pools.

Attachments: ingress_logs_1106.txt, lb-config-snapshot-1106.json (snapshots taken at 09:28 UTC).

Next steps: full post-incident diagnostics (we'll run kv cache & kernel telemetry checks) and propose a permanent route guard to prevent similar amplification.

I'll stay on the PD incident and post updates every 30 minutes until stable.

-Marcus
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference

Laura Bennett

From: Claire Dawson <claire@brizopay.com>

Thanks all — we saw the traffic batch come from a scheduled partner settlement at 08:42 UTC; we did have a short aggressive retry policy on that service which we've dialed back. After Marcus' team rotated the frontends and the rate-limit override, errors dropped quickly and our payment success rate recovered.

Appreciate the fast work and the RCA commitment. We'll review the post-mortem when available.

Claire
Director, Ops, Brizo Pay
